# 06 — Upstream pins

**Generated by `node tools/pins.mjs --write`. Do not edit by hand.**
`--check` fails when it is stale, because a pin nobody updates is worse
than no pin at all: it states a commit that was never built.

`third_party/` is not in this repository — it is other projects' code and
toolchains, none of it ours to redistribute. This file is what makes the
rest of the repository buildable: fetch each tree at the commit named
here, apply anything under `patches/`, then follow
[`02-ARCHITECTURE.md`](02-ARCHITECTURE.md).

The toolchain is **emscripten 4.0.18**, and that is not a suggestion:
SuperCollider's wasm build is pinned to it, and an older one fails in
ways that read as bugs in this project rather than as a version skew.

## Submodules, which a clone does not bring

`git clone` stops at the tree itself, and what a submodule carries goes
missing quietly rather than loudly — mi-UGens keeps libsamplerate this
way, and without it the build leaves MiBraids out on purpose, because a
UGen whose library is absent is worse than no UGen at all.

These are the ones populated in the trees that were built here. Any
other submodule in them was not needed by anything this project
compiles.

| Tree | Submodule |
|---|---|
| `DaisySP` | `DaisySP-LGPL` |
| `mi-UGens` | `projects/MiBraids/libsamplerate` |
| `sc3-plugins` | `external_libraries/nova-simd` |
| `sc3-plugins` | `external_libraries/stk` |
| `supercollider` | `editors/sc-el` |
| `supercollider` | `editors/scvim` |
| `supercollider` | `external_libraries/hidapi` |
| `supercollider` | `external_libraries/link` |
| `supercollider` | `external_libraries/nova-simd` |
| `supercollider` | `external_libraries/nova-tt` |
| `supercollider` | `external_libraries/portaudio/portaudio_submodule` |
| `supercollider` | `external_libraries/portmidi/portmidi_submodule` |
| `supercollider` | `external_libraries/utf8proc` |
| `supercollider` | `external_libraries/yaml-cpp` |

```
git -C third_party/DaisySP submodule update --init --recursive
git -C third_party/mi-UGens submodule update --init --recursive
git -C third_party/sc3-plugins submodule update --init --recursive
git -C third_party/supercollider submodule update --init --recursive
```

## `lua53`, a release tarball with a hash

The Lua runtime, and the whole of ADR-02: norns runs **Lua 5.3.6**, so
this does. `tools/lua53/build.sh` downloads it, refuses to unpack it unless
the hash matches, and compiles 33 translation units to `src/lua/lua53/`.
No patch — nothing in it needed changing. MIT.

```
https://www.lua.org/ftp/lua-5.3.6.tar.gz
sha256  fc5fd69bb8736323f026672b1b7235da613d7177e72558893a0bdcd320466d60
```

Until E9-117 this was **fengari**, Lua written in JavaScript, vendored from
npm and patched to 64-bit integers because its own were 32-bit. The patch
is gone with it: Lua's integers are 64-bit, and `test/integers.test.ts` —
which that patch is what created — still passes.
